metaDescription: Seven generator distribution boxes with GFCI outlets compared by inlet amp rating, outlet count, breakers and build, for job sites, campsites and outages.
expertTake: The Champion Pro Grade 50 amp box is the best all-rounder because every outlet has its own GFCI and overload protection and it adds a 30 amp locking outlet for a second cord. The GXELZK 30 amp box is the value pick for a mid-size generator. If you only plug in one or two cords, skip the box and use a single fan-style cord instead.
introParagraphs: A distribution box takes one heavy generator outlet and splits it into several protected household outlets. It is the tidy way to run tools or appliances from a portable generator without a nest of cords and adapters.

Boxes vary by inlet rating, outlet count, whether each outlet has its own breaker and whether the enclosure can stand up to rain and rough handling. Wiring them into a building is a different job, and this guide covers only portable plug-in units.

products.name: Champion Pro Grade 50A OSHA-style distribution box, six GFCI duplexes
products.description:
One 50 amp twist-lock inlet feeds six GFCI-protected 120 volt duplex outlets and one 120/240 volt 30 amp locking outlet. Each receptacle has its own overload protection and ground-fault protection, so a fault on a single tool trips only that outlet.

That per-outlet protection is what sets it apart from simpler boxes. A single GFCI on the inlet drops every tool on the site when one trips, while individually protected outlets let the rest of the crew keep working. The 30 amp locking outlet lets you daisy-chain a second box or feed a sub-cord.

A heavy-duty frame guards the box against being dragged and dropped. Keep the rubber covers shut when not in use, test every GFCI with its test button at the start of each day and store the box off the ground in the wet season. A tidy habit is to label each cord with the tool it feeds, so a tripped outlet leads you straight to the load that caused it. Because the box is large, carry it by the frame, not by the cords, which strains the inlet over time.
products.bestFor: Job sites and large outages where several people share one generator.
cons: Needs a 50A generator outlet and cord

products.name: Southwire Power X-Treme Box 50A with six 5-20 outlets
products.description:
The X-Treme Box is a steel temporary power box in the traditional job-site mould. It takes a 50 amp feed and splits it across six 5-20 outlets, with a 14 gauge steel shell that is built to endure years of site use.

Against the Champion Pro Grade, it is the older style: robust and simple, with fewer extras. Check the listing for GFCI details before you buy, since modern sites expect ground-fault protection on every outlet and the listing text emphasises construction rather than GFCI.

Steel is a strong point and a weight penalty. It will survive a dropped tool but is heavy to carry, and a dented case is still usable. Rust is the long-term enemy if it lives in a damp trailer. Wipe it dry after use and touch up chipped paint to slow corrosion. Over the years the outlets themselves wear before the shell does, so replace any receptacle that no longer grips a plug firmly.
products.bestFor: Rough job-site use where a steel shell matters.
cons: Listing text says little about GFCI

products.name: Spider box by Power Assemblies, 50A inlet and outlet, six 20A GFCI
products.description:
This is a spider-style box: a lightweight, non-conductive body with a 50 amp CS6375 inlet, a 50 amp CS6369 pass-through outlet and six 20 amp 125 volt GFCI outlets. NEMA 3R rated receptacle covers and branch circuit protection are listed.

The pass-through outlet is the clever part. It lets you chain a second box or feed a distant sub-cord without a splitter, which makes one generator serve a long work area. The body is stackable and light, which helps when you carry it from a truck.

A non-conductive shell resists electrical hazards, but it is plastic, so it will not shrug off a hard impact the way steel does. Keep the covers closed, and watch the cord strain relief where a heavy 50 amp cord meets the inlet. Chaining a second box through the pass-through adds the second box's load to the same feed, so the generator and the cord still set the real limit. Keep chained runs short to limit voltage drop.
products.bestFor: Crews that need to chain boxes and carry them often.
pros: Six GFCI outlets with branch protection
cons: Plastic is less impact tough than steel

products.name: GXELZK 30A temporary distribution box, four GFCI duplexes
products.description:
A 30 amp L14-30P plug feeds four NEMA 5-20R GFCI duplex outlets, eight receptacles in total. Built-in GFCI protection and a UL certification claim in the listing target construction-site use.

That layout matches a mid-size generator with an L14-30 outlet, and it is smaller and lighter than the 50 amp boxes. The tradeoff is capacity: a 30 amp feed at 250 volts gives about 3,750 watts per 120 volt leg, so spread tools across both legs.

Compared with the six-breaker 30 amp box below, it offers fewer protection points but a simpler face. Check the labelling when it arrives and test the GFCI before first use. Over time the plug on the inlet cord takes the abuse, so keep a spare cord on hand and inspect the strain relief each season. For a home user with a small generator, this size is also easy to carry from a garage shelf to the yard.
products.bestFor: Mid-size generator owners running a few tools or appliances.
pros: Four GFCI duplexes from one L14-30 plug
cons: Few breakers compared with larger boxes

products.name: 30A temporary distribution box with six breakers and locking outlets
products.description:
This box adds two locking outlets, an L14-30R and an L5-30R, to four GFCI duplexes, and protects each circuit with six individual breakers. The locking outlets let it feed a transfer-switch inlet cord or an RV adapter.

Compared with the GXELZK, the extra breakers give finer protection and the locking outlets give more ways to connect. It is the more flexible 30 amp box, at the cost of a slightly busier face.

Use the breakers deliberately: assign each tool a circuit and watch for trips, which tell you where the load is too high. The two outlet styles also make it useful beyond tool use: the L5-30R can feed a small RV adapter, and the L14-30R can feed a transfer inlet cord, so one box covers several roles. Label the breakers with the tool each one serves, and re-test each after a long storage period. Keep it dry between uses, since it is a lighter, less proven product and should be treated gently.
products.bestFor: Owners who need both household outlets and locking outlets from one 30A feed.
cons: Less detail in the listing than major brands
Capacity still limited by the 30A feed

products.name: Southwire Mini X-Treme 30A box, eight 5-20 outlets

specList.label: Concept
specList.value: Converts one L14-30P to eight outlets

products.description:
The Mini X-Treme converts one L14-30P inlet into eight NEMA 5-20R outlets, each with a 20 amp breaker and GFCI protection, split across the front and back panels. The NEMA Type 1 enclosure is for indoor or sheltered use.

Type 1 is the key limitation. It is not a wet-weather rating, so use it under cover or on a dry pad. Against the Champion Pro Grade, it is smaller and lighter, but offers less water protection.

It suits a garage or workshop where a generator sits outside and a short cord reaches the box. A good pick for a few tools and a fridge. With eight outlets on two faces, label which are on the front panel and which are on the back, so you can find the live ones quickly. Keep it off the floor to avoid splashes, and let it dry fully if it ever gets wet.
products.bestFor: Dry, sheltered workshops running a few tools from a 30A generator.
pros: Eight outlets from one L14-30P plug
GFCI and 20A breaker on each outlet
Compact for a shop bench or truck
cons: NEMA Type 1 is not a wet-weather rating

products.name: Zuomeng 30A portable power center, dual independent 120V circuits
products.description:
A 240 volt input is split into two independent 120 volt zones, A and B, each with its own GFCI outlets and control. Real-time power status monitoring is listed, which tells you whether each zone is live.

Splitting the feed into two zones addresses a real problem with 30 amp generators: balancing the legs. Putting heavy loads on zone A and lighter ones on zone B keeps you from tripping a single leg while the other sits idle.

It is the most controlled box in this lineup, which suits owners who want to switch zones on and off rather than pull plugs. Check the generator plug requirements in the listing before you order.
products.bestFor: Owners who want to control two 120V zones independently.
pros: Independent A and B zones with GFCI
Helps balance legs on a 30A feed
cons: Fewer outlet details in the listing
Less proven than long-running job-site boxes

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 50 amp inlet, as on the Champion Pro Grade and Southwire X-Treme, serves a large generator, while a 30 amp inlet like the GXELZK suits a mid-size one. Never feed a 50 amp box from a 30 amp generator through an adapter. Match the inlet to the generator outlet.

The Champion gives each receptacle its own GFCI and overload protection, and the Southwire Mini adds a 20 amp breaker per outlet. A box with one main GFCI drops everything when a single tool faults. Per-outlet protection keeps the rest running.

Eight outlets on the Mini X-Treme or twelve receptacles on a six-duplex box sound like a lot, but your generator limits what you can run. Count the tools you will actually plug in. Locking outlets, as on the six-breaker 30 amp box, let you feed further cords.

NEMA Type 1, as on the Mini X-Treme, is for dry locations. The Power Assemblies box lists NEMA 3R covers for light rain. If the box will sit outside, choose a rain-rated model and keep it off wet ground.

A 14 gauge steel shell like the Southwire X-Treme resists abuse but is heavy. A lightweight non-conductive body such as the Power Assemblies box is easy to carry but less impact tough. Pick by how rough your use will be.
A 30 amp 250 volt feed gives about 3,750 watts per 120 volt leg. The Zuomeng box exposes two zones so you can balance them on purpose. On any box, spread heavy loads across both legs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Protection design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared per-outlet GFCI and breakers across the lineup. The Champion Pro Grade and Southwire Mini X-Treme score highest here. Boxes with a single main protector lose points for tool crews.

howWeEvaluated.title: Inlet and generator fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated 30 and 50 amp boxes because their plugs do not interchange. A box must match the generator outlet. Adapters were treated as a weakness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Enclosure suitability
howWeEvaluated.description: We read enclosure ratings, from Type 1 to 3R covers, and the shell material. Steel resists impact and plastic resists corrosion. Wet-weather use points to 3R covers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Expandability
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited pass-through outlets such as the 50A CS6369 on the Power Assemblies box and the 30A locking outlet on the Champion. These let you chain boxes. Specs on the listing plus patterns in owner reports inform this call.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing evidence
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted UL claims on the GXELZK listing and construction detail on the Southwire. Claims we could not confirm count for less. We advise checking the label on arrival.

cards.label: Steel box
cards.text: The Southwire X-Treme uses 14 gauge steel that survives drops and drags. It is heavy and can rust in a damp trailer.

cards.label: Spider box
cards.text: The Power Assemblies box is light, non-conductive and stackable with a pass-through outlet. It tolerates impact less well than steel.

howToChoose.note: Choose steel for rough sites and a spider box when you carry and chain boxes.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: GFCI on every outlet, per-outlet breakers, a rain-rated cover and a frame that survives a drop. Test the GFCIs at the start of each shift.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Champion Pro Grade and Power Assemblies boxes list GFCI and branch protection on every outlet.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Several people share one generator or the site is wet, pointing to the Champion Pro Grade or the Power Assemblies 50A box.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You run two or three tools in a dry area, where the GXELZK 30A box is enough.

maintenance.why: A GFCI that fails to trip offers no protection. Use the test button before you rely on it.
Cracked jackets and bent pins cause heat. Replace damaged parts, not tape them.
Open covers admit rain and dust. Replace broken covers.

maintenance.task: Dry and store off the ground
maintenance.why: Water in a box corrodes contacts. Let it dry before storage.
Trip and reset each to confirm they work. A stuck breaker is a hazard.

faq.q: What does a generator distribution box do?
faq.a: It splits one generator outlet into several protected household outlets. Many include GFCI and individual breakers. It is the tidy way to run several tools or appliances.

faq.q: Do I need a 30 amp or 50 amp distribution box?
faq.a: Match the generator's outlet. A 30 amp box such as the GXELZK suits a mid-size generator with an L14-30 outlet. A 50 amp box such as the Champion Pro Grade suits a larger one.

faq.q: Can I use a distribution box for my house?
faq.a: A plug-in box powers tools and appliances, not house wiring. Feeding a house takes a transfer switch and a licensed electrician. Never backfeed through a wall outlet.

faq.q: Is GFCI on every outlet necessary?
faq.a: It is the safer layout, especially outdoors and on wet ground. The Champion and Power Assemblies boxes list GFCI on outlets. A single main GFCI protects less finely.

faq.q: How do I balance loads on a 30 amp box?
faq.a: A 30 amp 250 volt feed gives about 3,750 watts per 120 volt leg. Spread heavy loads across both legs. The Zuomeng box exposes two zones so you can do this deliberately.

faq.q: Can I leave a distribution box outside in the rain?
faq.a: Only a rain-rated one, and even then keep it off wet ground with covers closed. Type 1 enclosures like the Mini X-Treme are for dry spots. Bring it in after use.
